answer: Like stars dimming in a nebula, an agent's reputation can be made to decay with inactivity: every idle week shaves off a slice of earned trust, so a dormant identity cannot wake up as a haven for a sudden Sybil strike. An attacker must keep thousands of fake accounts constantly working to hold their standing, paying real compute and attention every day, while a single honest agent only needs its own steady record. Sleeping Sybils simply fade to worthless opal dust before they can attack.
